title: Exceptional-fibre gluing in two-generator regular-sequence blowup charts
statement:
Let $A$ be a commutative Noetherian ring, and let $x,y\in A$ be such that both $(x,y)$ and $(y,x)$ are regular sequences and $k=A/(x,y)$ is a field. Set $I=(x,y)$, $Y=\operatorname{Bl}_I(\operatorname{Spec}A)$ and $E=Y\times_{\operatorname{Spec}A}\operatorname{Spec}k$. On the standard blowup charts $U_x=D_+(xT)$ and $U_y=D_+(yT)$, with coordinates $t=(yT)/(xT)$ and $u=(xT)/(yT)$, the scheme-theoretic fibre has the canonical affine descriptions
$$E\cap U_x\cong\operatorname{Spec}k[t],\qquad E\cap U_y\cong\operatorname{Spec}k[u].$$
The scheme-theoretic overlap is $\operatorname{Spec}k[t,t^{-1}]$, identified with the basic opens $D(t)$ and $D(u)$ in those affine lines by $u=t^{-1}$. The chart maps $t\mapsto T_1/T_0$ and $u\mapsto T_0/T_1$ give compatible isomorphisms to the standard charts of $\mathbf P^1_k$, and glue, with their inverses, to a $k$-scheme isomorphism $E\cong\mathbf P^1_k$. The scheme $E$ is regular: every local ring at a point of either affine chart is the corresponding prime localization of $k[t]$ or $k[u]$ and is regular local.
Conventions: [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], [def-weil-pbc-regular-sequence], [def-nagata-global-blowup], [def-nagata-affine-proj], [def-nagata-affine-blowup-chart-map], [def-pc-fibre-product], [def-weil-affine-spectrum], [def-nagata-projective-space-base-change], [def-weil-regular-scheme], [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime].

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-two-parameter-blowup-atlas] to the commutative Noetherian ring $A$ and the two ordered regular sequences explicitly supplied in the hypotheses. The current atlas gives the cover $Y=U_x\cup U_y$, with $U_x=D_+(xT)$ and $U_y=D_+(yT)$, and the canonical $A$-algebra presentations $C_x=A[I/x]\cong A[t]/(xt-y)$ and $C_y=A[I/y]\cong A[u]/(yu-x)$. Its identifications send $t$ to $(yT)/(xT)$ and $u$ to $(xT)/(yT)$ and preserve the structure maps from $A$. Thus the tensor reductions in step 2 use these specified $A$-algebras and the overlap calculation in step 3 uses these specified homogeneous fractions. The atlas now also lists its affine-blowup, Rees-algebra, polynomial-ring and quotient-algebra conventions; none adds a local or regular-ring hypothesis on $A$.

source.place: Tag 0BIQ, lemma-blowup-regular-sequence, applied in both orders; atlas interface

proof.text: Write $p:E\to Y$ for the projection. By [lem-weil-pbc-open-fibre-product], $V_x=p^{-1}U_x=U_x\times_{\operatorname{Spec}A}\operatorname{Spec}k$ and $V_y=p^{-1}U_y$ are open subschemes of $E$ and cover it. By [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra], $V_x=\operatorname{Spec}(C_x\otimes_A k)$. Explicitly the $k$-algebra isomorphism $C_x\otimes_A k\to k[t]$ sends $[f(t)]\otimes\bar a$ to $\bar a\bar f(t)$, reducing every coefficient modulo $I$. It is well defined because $xt-y$ reduces to zero and is balanced over $A$. Its inverse sends $\bar a$ to $1\otimes\bar a$ and $t$ to $[t]\otimes1$. Both composites fix coefficients and the polynomial generator; on a pure tensor the inverse composite is $[f]\otimes\bar a$ by the balancing relation. Thus it is an isomorphism. The same formulas with $u$ give $C_y\otimes_A k\cong k[u]$. These are scheme-theoretic fibre calculations, without replacing a fibre by its set of points.

source.place: Tags 01JR (lemma-open-fibre-product), 01I4 (lemma-fibre-product-affine-schemes); explicit reduction of the presentations of Tag 0BIQ

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-proj-basic-open-intersection] to the Rees algebra with $f=xT$, $g=yT$, both of degree one. The overlap in $U_x$ is $D(t)$, and in $U_y$ it is $D(u)$. Pulling back to $E$ gives these same basic opens in $V_x,V_y$: a local ring map carries a unit to a unit, and if an element is a nonunit of a local ring it is in the maximal ideal and its image under a local map is a nonunit. Hence taking the inverse image of a basic open gives the basic open of the pulled-back function. By [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-section-vanishing-prime] their rings are $k[t]_t$ and $k[u]_u$. In the common homogeneous localization, the fraction representatives of [def-nagata-homogeneous-localization-degree-zero] satisfy $((yT)/(xT))((xT)/(yT))=1$. Thus the transition sends $u$ to $t^{-1}$; it fixes $A$ and after reduction fixes $k$. Explicitly $k[u]_u\to k[t]_t$ sends $u$ to $t^{-1}$ and $u^{-1}$ to $t$, with inverse sending $t$ to $u^{-1}$ and $t^{-1}$ to $u$. The composites fix the displayed generators. Writing $k[t,t^{-1}]=k[t]_t$ proves the claimed scheme-theoretic overlap and its two inclusions.

source.place: Tags 01M4 (lemma-standard-open), 01MA (lemma-standard-open-proj); schemes.tex Tags 01I3 and 01HV for principal opens and their rings

proof.text: Use [lem-weil-pbc-projective-space-standard-charts] for $S=\operatorname{Spec}k$ and the homogeneous index set $\{0,1\}$. The two opens $P_0,P_1$ cover $P=\mathbf P^1_k$ and have rings $k[v]$, $v=T_1/T_0$, and $k[w]$, $w=T_0/T_1$. On the universal projective space over $\mathbf Z$, [lem-weil-pbc-proj-basic-open-intersection] identifies their overlap as $D(v)=D(w)$ in these respective charts; pulling this open back to $k$ gives the same description, by the unit test used in step 3. By [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-section-vanishing-prime] this overlap is affine with ring $k[v]_v$ in $P_0$ and $k[w]_w$ in $P_1$, so morphisms into it and the restrictions of the chart maps to it are determined by ring maps on these localizations. The homogeneous fractions have $vw=1$, so their transition is $w=v^{-1}$. The coefficient-fixing polynomial isomorphisms $k[t]\to k[v]$, $t\mapsto v$, and $k[u]\to k[w]$, $u\mapsto w$, and their inverses induce affine $k$-scheme isomorphisms by [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. On overlaps the ring square commutes: either path sends $u$ to $v^{-1}$ and fixes $k$; its inverse square commutes as well. Thus both the local scheme maps $V_x\to P_0$, $V_y\to P_1$ and their inverses agree on overlaps.

source.place: Tag 01NG (lemma-standard-covering-projective-space), Tag 01M4 (lemma-standard-open); coordinate comparison with resolve.tex Tag 0AGQ

proof.text: Compose the two local maps with $P_0,P_1\hookrightarrow P$. By [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-morphism-gluing] they give $F:E\to P$. Apply the same theorem to the inverse maps followed by $V_x,V_y\hookrightarrow E$, obtaining $G:P\to E$. On $V_x$ and $V_y$, respectively, $GF$ is the composite of the corresponding inverse affine isomorphisms, hence the identity. The uniqueness clause of that theorem gives $GF=\mathrm{id}_E$. On $P_0,P_1$ it similarly gives $FG=\mathrm{id}_P$. Each local map fixes the coefficient ring $k$; therefore its composite with the structure map to $\operatorname{Spec}k$ is the original structure map on that open. Uniqueness under gluing makes both global maps morphisms over $k$. This gives the required $k$-scheme isomorphism with the stated chart formulas.

The field hypothesis on $k$ permits [lem-sc-p1-polynomial-regular]: both $k[t]$ and $k[u]$ are Noetherian regular rings. Every point of $E$ belongs to $V_x$ or $V_y$. By [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-stalk-localization], its local ring is canonically the localization of that chart ring at its corresponding prime. It is regular local by the cited regular-ring statement, including the zero prime. The two regular affine neighbourhoods therefore make $E$ regular by [def-weil-regular-scheme].
